messages:
maria: heads up — after today's canary we saw a 4x bump in payload-shape rejects for the external-invoke route. spike started ~08:12 UTC.
chris: ack. console shows a general error-rate increase but not why. do we have telemetry that differentiates reject reasons?
olivia: current dashboard only has a single counter 'validation_failed'. no subtype or shape id. makes triage painful.
maria: exactly. we need at least validation_error_type + an anonymized example hash. no PII.
kai: +1 to hash + type. also tag by routing policy and quota tier so we can see if reserved pools are affected.
neil: short question — when a payload fails validation today do we auto-fallback to a generation path or surface an error upstream?
maria: today we return error to caller immediately. no fallback. that caused client retries and quota burn for some customers.
chris: that aligns with the spike in quota usage. propose: for non-critical rejects, route to a lenient runtime path that strips the offending tool fields and returns a warning envelope.
olivia: UX ask: console should show a 'payload rejects' timeline with drilldowns: shape_hash, first-seen, top-slices by rollout slice. also quick-bisect link to diffs between rollout slices.
maria: telemetry sketch: counters named `action.rejects.{error_type}.{shape_hash}.{route}.{quota_tier}` plus a small sample of example_payload_hash per shape, and histogram of latency on rejects.
kai: ops concern: that increases cardinality a lot. we should sample example_payload_hash and cap unique shape_hash ingest per minute.
chris: agree. implement an adaptive sampler: record everything low-res, but keep top-K shapes (e.g., top 50 in last hour) with full samples. alert on any new shape >5/min.
maria: example of one invalid response we observed:
```n{"tool_result": "OK", "meta": "unexpected_array"}
```
expected shape: `{"tool_result": {"status": "ok", "items": [...]} }`
neil: deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary 0.15 -> 1% :white_check_mark:
olivia: action items: (1) telemetry PR (maria), (2) console tile mock + bisect flow (olivia), (3) fallback policy spec (chris), (4) sampling + cardinality guard (kai). I'll file tickets.
maria: created ticket https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFR-3141 for telemetry work.
chris: drafting fallback RFC now, will ping when ready.
kai: PoC sampler landing later today, will post link.
olivia: thanks — please keep updates here. :thumbsup:
